newsitem.title: MEXICO: RESEARCH ALERT-Year-end peso forecast revised up.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Year-end peso forecast revised up.

text.p: Morgan Stanley Dean Witter said in a research report on Monday it had revised its year-end forecast exchange rate for the Mexican peso against the dollar sharply higher.
-- Analyst Ernest Brown said the brokerage now predicted the peso would trade at 8.30 per dollar by year's end, or considerably stronger than the previous estimate of 9.00 per dollar.
-- "We believe that a variety of political and economic factors are likely to keep the peso strong for a long period of time," Brown wrote.
-- Brown said the "reduced quotient of political risk" was the salient political factor in the wake of Sunday's mid-term elections.

-- "While the international press is focusing on the loss of political ground by the (ruling) PRI party, which seems to be losing its majority in the lower house of the Mexican Congress, we think the broader success story of political transition is more important," Brown added.
